# CLAUDE.md

Rules for agents working in this repository. Each id names a statement in the stmt store, the source of truth; read one with `stmt get ID`.

## agentic

- Every write made with an API token first asks the stmt gate in the channel's scope (operations such as editorial.write); BLOCK or INDETERMINATE refuses it with 403, and a successful write emits its AFTER event, so stmt rules decide and record what agents may do. (`agentic.gate`)
- Every POST that creates something accepts an Idempotency-Key header, except token creation: its secret is shown once and never stored, so a lost response means revoking that token and creating another. A repeat with the same key and body returns the stored response with Idempotent-Replayed: true; the same key with a different body is refused with 422, and a key whose first request is still running with 409. Keys expire after 24 hours. (`agentic.idempotency`)
- Agents authenticate with personal API tokens: prefixed `sre_`, stored only as hashes, expiring (default 90 days, at most 365), revocable, and limited to explicit scopes. A token never grants more than its user's role, and only a signed-in session can create, list or revoke tokens. (`agentic.tokens.scoped`)
- Writes made with an API token record the token as author (stmt owner type `token`, id = token id); the token record names its user. (`agentic.audit`)
- Replaceable resources return an ETag. PUT, PATCH and DELETE on them accept If-Match and answer 412 when the resource changed, so an agent never overwrites a change it has not seen. (`agentic.concurrency.etag`)
- Every JSON error is an RFC 9457 problem (application/problem+json) with type, title, status, detail and instance. `detail` stays the human-readable English message; validation errors add an `errors` list naming each field. (`agentic.errors.problem`)
- An MCP server at /mcp exposes the main operations as tools. Tools call the service layer, never HTTP routes or SQL, authenticate with the same API tokens and enforce the same roles and scopes. (`agentic.mcp`)
- MCP clients such as claude.ai connect with OAuth 2.1 as the MCP authorization spec describes: the 401 from /mcp points to protected-resource metadata, and the app is its own authorization server with dynamic client registration, authorization code with PKCE (S256) and a consent page where the signed-in person picks the scopes. Approving issues an ordinary sre_ API token named after the client, so roles, scopes, expiry, revocation, the gate, audit and rate limits apply unchanged. (`agentic.oauth`)
- The OAuth endpoints (/.well-known metadata, /oauth/register, /oauth/token) follow the OAuth RFCs instead of the API conventions: errors are {error, error_description} as RFC 6749 defines, and registration takes no Idempotency-Key. Redirect URIs must be https or a loopback http address and match exactly; codes are single-use, expire in 10 minutes and are stored only as hashes. (`agentic.oauth.protocol`)
- Every API operation has a stable snake_case operationId, a summary and a description written for an agent choosing which call to make. (`agentic.openapi.described`)
- List endpoints are paginated: `limit` (default 50, at most 200) and an opaque `cursor`; responses are {items, next_cursor}. (`agentic.pagination`)
- Each API token may make at most SREDITOR_AGENT_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE requests a minute (default 120), counted together across the API and /mcp; signed-in sessions are not counted. Every 429 response carries a Retry-After header: the whole seconds until a request is allowed again. (`agentic.rate-limits`)
- Every MCP tool has a human title and declares all four annotations explicitly: readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint and openWorldHint (false, since tools act only inside sreditor). An undeclared hint defaults to the worst case, so a tool that only creates or edits would otherwise reach clients as destructive. (`agentic.mcp.annotations`)
- An MCP tool that fails returns a tool error (isError) the agent can act on: what went wrong, the field or value at fault and the call that fixes it, such as the tool that lists valid ids. Protocol errors are only for malformed requests. (`agentic.mcp.errors`)
- MCP tools return structured content that matches a declared output schema, and list tools page with the same limit and cursor as the API (agentic.pagination), so no result floods the agent's context. (`agentic.mcp.results`)
- Follow the current MCP specification (2026-07-28): /mcp is stateless Streamable HTTP with JSON responses and keeps no session between requests, so any instance can answer any call. New code adopts none of the deprecated features: Roots, Sampling, Logging, the HTTP+SSE transport and, for clients that can use CIMD, dynamic client registration. (`agentic.mcp.spec`)
- MCP tool names, descriptions and schemas are fixed in code and never built from stored data, so text that people write, such as research notes, sources or screenplays, can never change what an agent is told a tool does. (`agentic.mcp.static-descriptions`)
- Design MCP tools around tasks an agent finishes in one or two calls, not one tool per HTTP route, and keep the set small. A tool's description says when to use it, when not to and what must exist first, for an agent choosing between tools. (`agentic.mcp.tools.outcomes`)
- The authorization server accepts Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD), the MCP default: it advertises client_id_metadata_document_supported, fetches an https client_id URL with SSRF protection (no private, loopback or link-local addresses; size and time limits), checks the document's client_id matches the URL and lists the redirect URI, and caches it as HTTP headers allow. Dynamic registration stays for older clients. Metadata also advertises authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported. (`agentic.oauth.cimd`)

## agents

- Run subagents on Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5). (`agents.subagent.model`)

## deployment

- Deploy on Docker: ship every service as a Docker image. (`deploy.docker`)
- The development deployment is published at https://sreditor-dev.arc4d3.com through the Cloudflare tunnel sreditor-development (zone arc4d3.com); SREDITOR_PUBLIC_URL must match it, and `sreditor doctor` checks that it answers. Production subdomains stay one level deep (name.arc4d3.com), because the free certificate covers only *.arc4d3.com. (`deploy.dev.url`)
- Observe the app with Prometheus, Loki and Grafana in compose.yaml under the observability profile: the app serves request metrics labelled by route template on SREDITOR_METRICS_PORT, a port the tunnel never routes to; Grafana Alloy ships container logs to Loki; Grafana provisions both sources and the dashboards in deploy/observability, and only Grafana publishes a port, on loopback, behind a login. (`deploy.observability`)

## documentation

- Generate every document from the stmt store, the single source of truth. Never edit a generated document by hand: revise the statement and regenerate. (`docs.generated.from.stmt`)

## engineering

- Build HTTP APIs with FastAPI. (`code.api.fastapi`)
- Write all code and schemas in English, including identifiers, comments, and table, column and field names. (`code.language.english`)
- Define data models and schemas with Pydantic models. (`code.models.pydantic`)
- Keep test coverage above 90%. (`code.tests.coverage`)
- Never hard-code paths, URLs or secrets: read them from settings ([tool.sreditor] in pyproject.toml or environment variables via Pydantic settings). (`code.config.no-hardcoded`)
- Never use a bare except or swallow an exception silently: catch specific exceptions and either handle them or re-raise with context. (`code.errors.explicit`)
- Format and lint all Python with Ruff; CI fails on any ruff format or ruff check violation. (`code.style.ruff`)
- Type-annotate every function signature; the code must pass a strict type check (mypy --strict). (`code.types.strict`)
- Commit no dead code: no commented-out code, unused imports or unreachable branches. (`code.dead.none`)
- Give a function at most 5 parameters; group related parameters into a Pydantic model. (`code.functions.args`)
- Keep functions short and single-purpose: cyclomatic complexity at most 10 and about 40 lines at most. (`code.functions.small`)
- Keep layers separate: API routes hold no SQL or business logic and call the store/repository layer, which never imports FastAPI. (`code.layers.separation`)
- Name things for what they are or do: no abbreviations or single-letter names outside comprehensions, and booleans read as predicates (is_, has_). (`code.naming.intent`)
- Write comments that explain why, not what; give every public module, class and function a one-line docstring. (`code.comments.why`)
- Prefer frozen Pydantic models and pure functions; keep side effects such as database and filesystem access at the edges. (`code.immutability`)
- Use no magic numbers or strings: name them as module constants or enums. (`code.magic.none`)
- Make each test check one behaviour and name it after that behaviour: test_<unit>_<condition>_<expected>. Exception: a flow test follows one user journey across several pages (registration, password reset, invitation, sign in and out, and the e2e tests) and may check each step in order; name it after the journey and its outcome. (`code.tests.naming`)

## i18n

- Mark every user-facing string for translation (_() in templates, N_() in Python) and keep its pt-BR entry in src/sreditor/locales/pt-BR.json; tests fail when a marked string has no translation or a translation has no marked string. (`i18n.catalog`)
- Write every user-facing text in English, the base language, and translate it into Brazilian Portuguese (pt-BR), the alternate language; English is the fallback for any missing translation. (`i18n.languages`)
- Keep the JSON API's error details and field names in English; only text meant for people (pages and emails) is translated. (`i18n.api.english`)
- Choose the language from the ?lang= switch, remembered in a cookie, then the Accept-Language header, then English; set <html lang> to it and send emails in the same language. (`i18n.negotiation`)
- Translate stmt prose shown to users, such as terms and privacy, in a sibling category suffixed with the lowercase locale (terms.pt-br); pages fall back to the English category when it is empty. (`i18n.prose`)

## project

- A social account (its platform and handle, ignoring a leading @ and letter case) belongs to at most one channel. A second channel claiming it is refused with 409 and told only that another channel holds it, never which, since channels stay private to their members. (`project.accounts.unique`)
- An episode belongs to one channel, is numbered within it and moves through the statuses idea, research, script, production and published. Its parts (editorial research, sources and waivers, screenplay, characters, locations, voice-over, sound, visual) are added one step at a time and each is stored and revised on its own, so editing one part never conflicts with another; characters, locations and visual style live in a channel library that episodes refer to. (`project.episodes`)
- An episode refers to its channel library by name: a character who speaks in its screenplay, or a place a scene heading names, matches the library entry with the same name ignoring case and spacing. A name with no entry is offered for adding and never added on its own, so typos do not fill the library. (`project.library.by-name`)
- An episode's media are files: voice-over, sound effects and score as audio (MP3, WAV or M4A) and visual effects as video (MP4 or WebM), at most SREDITOR_MAX_MEDIA_BYTES (default 95 MB, under Cloudflare's 100 MB request limit) each. The type comes from the file's content, never its name; a file is copied to disk in chunks, never held whole in memory. Each file has a name and a note people can change; the file itself never changes, so a new take is a new file. (`project.media`)
- A channel keeps pitches (pautas): story ideas with a title, a summary and a status (idea, research, approved, discarded), each with its own research notes and sources, stored and revised on their own. An episode may reference one pitch, and a pitch may feed several episodes; an episode shows its pitch's notes and sources as they are, never a copy, next to its own research. A pitch that episodes reference cannot be deleted until they drop it. (`project.pitches`)
- sreditor is a social media channel manager and production tool: it manages channels, their accounts on each social platform, their brand kits and their Editorial guidelines, and produces their episodes, from research and screenplay to voice-over, sound and visuals. Build features in service of that purpose. (`project.purpose`)
- A channel's library also holds visual styles: a name and a description of the look (palette, framing, type, motion). Each episode picks at most one style from its own channel's library, stored and revised on its own; removing a style from the library leaves the episodes that used it without one. (`project.visual-style`)
- An episode's waivers are the signed releases behind it (image, voice or location rights): a PDF, JPEG or PNG file of at most SREDITOR_MAX_MEDIA_BYTES with who signed, when and what it covers. They hold personal data, so only owners and editors see or change them; a token reads them only with the waivers:read scope and changes them only with editorial:write as well. Their files always download, never display inline. (`project.waivers`)

## repository

- Keep the repository ready to publish on GitHub: a README, a LICENSE file and a .gitignore, with no secrets or local build artifacts committed. (`repo.github.ready`)
- License the project under the MIT License. (`repo.license.mit`)

## ui

- Build every page from the shared design system: Jinja macros in templates/_ui.html plus their CSS (button, field, card, alert, tag and so on). Add a new component there before using it, and show every component, in each state, theme and language, on a /design page that only runs in development. (`ui.design-system`)
- Cover every public flow with Playwright in a real browser (register, verify, sign in and out, password reset, invitation, language switch) and the signed-in journey (create a channel, add an account, upload a brand file, write editorial, create and edit an episode, research it with a source and a pitch, write the screenplay, add its cast, upload a voice-over and a waiver, add and pick a visual style, invite, create a token, delete the channel) against the Docker build; a flow is done when its e2e passes. (`ui.e2e.playwright`)
- Define every color, spacing step, radius, font size, shadow, duration and easing curve once, as design tokens (CSS custom properties) in src/sreditor/web/static/tokens.css, with light and dark values; components use only tokens, never raw values. (`ui.tokens`)
- Make every e2e run save evidence: a Playwright screenshot of each step at mobile (390px) and desktop (1280px) widths, in light and dark themes and in English and pt-BR, plus a trace for each failure. Write it to a git-ignored folder and attach it to the pull request. (`ui.e2e.evidence`)
- Give every action visible feedback: hover, focus-visible, pressed, loading (a submit button shows it is working and cannot be pressed twice), success and error states. Never leave the user guessing whether something happened. (`ui.microinteractions`)
- Animate with the motion tokens only: short durations (100-300 ms) and gentle easing curves (ease-out to enter, ease-in to leave), animating transform and opacity rather than layout; turn non-essential motion off under prefers-reduced-motion. Exception: a loading indicator turns for as long as its request runs, at its own token (--duration-spin); it is essential feedback, so it keeps turning under prefers-reduced-motion. (`ui.motion`)
- Ship polished UI: consistent spacing on the token scale, aligned edges, WCAG AA contrast in both themes, visible keyboard focus, no layout shift while loading, and layouts that work from 360px wide upward. (`ui.polish`)

## voice

- Trate o usuário pelo nome: Pedro. (`voice.address-by-name`)
- Não traga informações sem contexto; sempre deixe claro de onde vêm as informações. (`voice.cite-sources`)
- Peça decisão ao Pedro só quando ela importa para ele: produto, custo, segurança, dados de usuários, algo difícil de desfazer ou que muda como ele usa o sistema. Em escolhas técnicas internas, siga sua recomendação, faça e conte o que foi feito. (`voice.decide-what-matters`)
- Explique o problema, as causas, as possíveis soluções e suas consequências, e aponte sua recomendação. (`voice.explain-then-recommend`)
- Liste as opções como A, B, …; a opção recomendada fica em negrito. (`voice.options-format`)
- Use linguagem simples, sem termos desnecessários ou complexos; o usuário é inteligente. (`voice.plain-language`)

## web

- Registration and password-reset pages show the same response whether or not the email has an account. (`web.auth.no-enumeration`)
- Every email that carries a token links to the matching page with the token in the fragment (#token=), which browsers never send to servers; the page copies it into its form and removes it from the address bar, and without JavaScript the person pastes the whole link into the form. Never ask a user to call an API endpoint by hand. (`web.email.links`)
- Protect every state-changing form with a CSRF token (double-submit cookie) and reject a POST whose Origin header does not match the public URL. (`web.forms.csrf`)
- Build the public, unauthenticated area as server-rendered pages in the FastAPI app, with Jinja2 templates and HTMX, served from the same origin and Docker image as the API; do not add a separate frontend service for it. (`web.public.server-rendered`)
- Serve public pages with a self-only Content-Security-Policy and X-Frame-Options: DENY, and vendor static assets such as htmx locally instead of loading them from a CDN. (`web.security.headers`)
- Registration requires explicit consent to the terms of service and privacy policy, published at /terms and /privacy. (`web.signup.consent`)
- Opening a link that carries a token only renders a form; consume the token only on that form's POST, so email link scanners cannot spend it. (`web.tokens.post-only`)
- Brand files and episode media are stored by the AssetStore under SREDITOR_ASSETS_DIR (a Docker volume), named by content hash, and served only to channel members and only while the kit or an episode references them, with the security headers and a private immutable cache; images and episode media display inline, other files download. (`web.app.assets`)
- After a change, a signed-in page redirects (303, or HX-Redirect for htmx) so a reload does not repeat it, and the next page says what happened from a short-lived cookie that holds only a message key; a failed change re-renders the form with each error next to its field. (`web.app.feedback`)
- Put the signed-in pages in src/sreditor/web/workspace/, one module per area (channels, accounts, brand, editorial, episodes, library, members, account) with templates in templates/workspace/; they render server-side with Jinja2 and htmx like the public pages, call the service and store layer, and are left out of the OpenAPI schema. (`web.app.layout`)
- The signed-in area at /app lists the person's channels and offers, per channel, an overview with what it still needs, accounts, brand kit, editorial, episodes, the library of characters and locations, and members, plus settings for editors; /app/account holds the profile, password and API tokens. A new area adds one entry to the channel's menu. (`web.app.pages`)
- Signed-in pages need a session and send a visitor without one to sign in and back. A channel the person is not a member of answers 404, as the API does; actions their role does not allow are hidden, and their POST answers 403. (`web.app.permissions`)
- Forms show validation, rate-limit and expired-token errors next to the relevant field; the JSON endpoints stay unchanged for API clients. (`web.forms.errors`)
- Put the public pages in src/sreditor/web/: routes.py, Pydantic form models in forms.py, templates/ and static/; page routes call the store and service layer, never SQL. (`web.layout`)
- The public area offers /, /register, /register/sent, /verify, /login, /forgot-password, /reset-password, /invitations/{token}, /terms and /privacy; a signed-in visitor to / is redirected to the app. (`web.public.pages`)
